text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL FACILITATES MERCOSUR IMPORTS
Under pressure from its Mercosur partners, particularly Argentina, the Brazilian government on Wednesday altered the country's new import financing rules.

Brazil changed the definition of paying "in cash" for imports from Mercosur countries, effectively lengthening the time importers have to pay for imported goods. It also decided to make an exemption for Mercosur imports up to a value of $40,000 if they are backed by guarantees from their respective central banks using so-called CCR contracts.
-- ROBERTO SETUBAL TO HEAD FEBRABAN

Roberto Setubal, president of Banco Itau, will head the Brazilian Federation of Banks (Febraban). Setubal will replace Mauricio Schulman, former president of Banco Bamerindus, which was partially absorbed by HSBC Holdings Plc.
-- TELEBRAS KNOCKED DOWN BY MOTTA'S COMMENTS
Telebras subscription receipts fell on the stock exchanges after Communications Minister Sergio Motta's remarks against the conversion of subscription receipts into the company's shares.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- MAJORITY IN SAO PAULO WANTS LAYOFFS IN SECURITY OFFICE
The majority of Sao Paulo citizens thinks state governor Mario Covas should sack top officials at the state's security office due to the involvement of 10 police officers in deaths and tortures.
-- MOTTA ATTACKS COVAS, CHURCH AND MINISTERS

Communications Minister Sergio Motta, speaking for five hours at a seminar on telecommunications privatizations, attacked Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas, ministers, the church and the administrative reform.
O GLOBO
-- MAGALHAES IMPOSES RULES FOR BREAKING BANK SECRECY AT CPI

Senate president Antonio Carlos Magalhaes intervened in a congressional inquiry into a multi-million state debt scam by leading senators to approve rules for breaking the bank secrecy of those allegedly involved in the scandal.
-- BAND A CELLULAR ASSETS TO BE SOLD OFF SOON

The government will speed up the privatization of the Band A cellular assets. Communications Minister Sergio Motta said the government was concerned the upcoming selloff of Band B cellular concessions would expose the Band A services to ferocious competition and undermine their value.
- - - -- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
